newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis down 1/8 to 1/4 pt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis down 1/8 to 1/4 pt.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds slipped 1/8 point to 1/4 point in light midday action, but cheaper levels appeared to be sparking some business.

"There was a couple of secondary going away trades yesterday, so at the adjusted levels we are starting to see some life," one trader said. "Tuesday we were just dead. Yesterday, it started to spike a little bit, and today with the adjusted levels we are starting to see some business come in institutionally."
The trader said municipals have probably weakened 10 basis points from the week's start.
A second trader said munis appeared to be moving in tandem with U.S. Treasuries as players paused to regroup.

"I think they are just wondering where the market is going," he said. "It's looking a little weak in here, but other than that nothing is going on. It's a Thursday and a lot of the big deals are gone. So people are just kind of reassessing what they are going to do."
The trader believes yields are headed higher, he said.

"I mean Canada just raised rates, Japan is saying their economy is going well, and they might raise rates," he said. "So I mean if all the other countries are going to start raising rates, you've got to keep balance."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 9/32 at 98-8/32 to yield 6.76 percent. On the economic front, the Labor Department said initial state jobless claims fell to 332,000 in the week ended June 21, from a revised 346,000 the prior week.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 10/32 at 116-28/32. The September T-bond contract was down 11/32 at 111-12/32. The MOB spread was 176 ticks.
Thursday's new issues included a $346 million Philadelphia Airport bond deal, which Lehman Brothers tentatively priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2018.
Bear Stearns & Co tentatively priced $100 million Utah County, Utah, hospital revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2026.
Lehman also tentatively priced a $65 million Sarasota County, Fla., hospital deal. The bonds came at a top yield of 5.60 percent in 2020.
